packages.note: You own tools/pipeline/pipe_fist.py, the collar keys of tools/pipeline/blender_parts.py, assets/*/characters/punk/**, assets/source/palette/punk.json (slot 19 only), the Punk rows of tests/test_art_contract.gd and tests/test_art_punk.gd, game/actors/art/punk_art.tres and its variants, the ASSETS.md Punk rows, docs/milestones/M4-calls/F-punk.md and ARCHITECTURE's F-punk heading. Everything else is someone else's. (1) THE CUFF. Look first at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-arachne-repos-beat-em-up-PoC/097d610a-a8fb-4633-bbe9-6486aed195e7/scratchpad/fpfix/pair_gloves_c2.png (bottom half: today) beside the concept. Today's collar is a wide flat flange under each fist (8.6 cm from the arm's axis): it reads as a plunger or joystick base and is the biggest thing in the guard at 1 m that the concept doesn't have. The concept's cuff is a dark band about as wide as the back of the glove, hugging the wrist and rising a few centimetres up the forearm, with at most a slight flare at its top. Reshape build_collar to that: a band that follows the forearm's own outline with a small margin (a few mm, your call from the stills), gets its size from its LENGTH up the forearm rather than its radius, has a rolled rim, and blends into the glove's back with no shelf. Keep what F1 got right: the glove's dark slot, no ink on the collar, no slivers or needles, the arm's trim under it, the collar left out of the UV2 unwrap. THE BAR: F1 found that A9's 4 pp lens-share bar is what forced the flange, because the art covers less of the view than the proxies' forearm and fist box in the strikes (the cross at +8 degrees: art 29.1%, proxies 32.9%). The lead's call: the cuff follows the concept, not M3's primitive box. Get the share back through the band's length where it reads naturally; if the concept's cuff still misses 4 pp in some poses, ship the concept's cuff, make each missing pose's share a ratchet at its new figure (plus a small margin), print the plan's exact bar as a GATE line as lock 3 does for the cells, and list the poses and numbers. Rebuild the three variants the same way so they stay comparable (punk_rest, punk_auto, punk_auto_rest). (2) THE LENS A/B. The concept's lenses are gold in a dark frame. F-punk-fix made the lens cream (#e6dcc4) because the cap's yellow made the head one mass; the dark frame exists now. Record C1 ('Look: Punk face at 1 m') and C6 ('Look: distances') with slot 19 back at the cap's yellow #e8bd2e (still 6 colours; regenerate the atlas with tools/pipeline/gen_palette.py) and compare with the cream at 1, 2.5, 5 and 10 m. Keep the yellow if the dark frame clearly separates the lens from the cap at 1 m and 2.5 m (cap, frame line, lens, frame line, face, as in the concept); otherwise keep the cream. If the yellow wins, change test_the_punks_shades_are_a_marks_off_lens_in_a_dark_frame_apart_from_the_cap so it asserts the separation through the dark frame faces above and below the lens instead of a colour distance, and log the assertion old -> new with why; keep the lens marks-off either way. Make a side-by-side still of both lenses at 1 m and at 2.5 m for the lead. THEN: re-export over punk.glb, run tools/pipeline/run.py --check (and the heat-map build's), regenerate the palette atlas, run the full suite (green, 0 SCRIPT ERROR, SHADER ERROR or ERROR; the only acceptable change to an A9 assertion is the ratchet above, logged old -> new), and re-record C1, C2 ('Look: Punk body at 1 m'), C4 ('Look: Punk attacks at 1 m') and C11 ('Look: hold the Punk'), one act per process. Done: full-resolution crops of the guard (C2), the jab and cross (C4) and the hold (C11) beside the concept and beside F-punk-fix's 'after' crop, with an honest read: does the glove now read as the concept's fingerless glove on a wrist cuff?
